messages:
alex: Pushed a quick profiling dump from last night's canary. Seeing a weird tail: kernel selection flips to the 'long-seq optimized' kernels under continuous batching and latency spikes for 1-2 requests consistently. attaching summary below.

alex: summary: median p95 latency +18% when sequences are mixed (short+long) vs uniform short. throughput OK.

rachel: ugh. do you have the batch composition histogram? this sounds like launch overhead + kernel warmup.

alex: attaching histogram snippet: 
```
batch_sizes: [1,2,4,8]
sequence_len_hist: { <=64: 62%, 65-256: 28%, >256: 10% }
kernel_choice_log: [small-kernel, small-kernel, long-kernel, long-kernel]
```
we switch to long-kernel when average seq len > ~80 (autotuner threshold).

sam: can you dump the kernel launch timing (ms) around the switch? my hypothesis: long-kernel has bigger launch/setup cost; continuous batching groups mixed inputs which increases latency for short ones waiting for KV cache prep.

alex: here's a quick trace from perf-bot: 
```
[0.0] receive request (len 12)
[0.2] batch wait -> batched with 6 other reqs
[0.5] autotuner picked long-kernel (threshold triggered)
[0.5] kernel setup 3.2ms
[3.8] first token emitted -> short reqs see added 3ms
```

jia: thanks. that aligns with what I saw in the simulator. two levers: (1) adjust autotuner to prefer small-kernel when majority are short even if mean > threshold, (2) add a quick fast-path for tiny sequences that bypasses long-kernel.

rachel: option (1) sounds safer. autotuner currently uses mean seq length and historical perf. we could change scoring to use percentile (e.g., 75th) or weighted median to avoid being pulled by a few long sequences. also consider including kernel launch cost into the autotune scoring function.

sam: +1 on adding launch overhead to score. also need to consider KV cache behavior: long-kernel uses a different KV layout that invalidates cached pointers for some model configs which causes extra mem copies on first invocation. that could be contributing. we need to mark that in the profiler traces.

alex: good catch — trace shows an extra memcpy on first token for long-kernel path: ~1.7ms. combining that with 3ms setup explains the spike.

jia: proposed quick experiments:
- A: autotuner change -> use 75th percentile for seq len and add a static penalty for kernel switch if mixed batch ratio < 0.2
- B: introduce tiny-seq fast-path (<32 tokens) that always picks small-kernel with minimal setup
- C: measure impact of deferring kernel switch until batch boundary vs immediate switch (i.e., keep current kernel for 1 more batch if switching cost > benefit)

rachel: can someone run A and C on canary? A should be quick. C needs a controlled replay.

sam: I'll run A on canary now with a flag: `AUTOTUNE_SEQ_PERCENTILE=75; KERNEL_SWITCH_PENALTY_MS=5` and collect p95/throughput.

perf-bot: scheduled job 1769204330: canary-autotune-A (24h) started by sam. logs -> /infra/artifacts/1769204330.tar.gz

alex: thanks. I'll prep a targeted replay for C using the mixed-seq trace and test deferred-switch policy. expect results by EOD.

jia: long term we should teach the autotuner to be batch-composition-aware: classify batch as "mostly-short" and score kernels by per-token latency for the short slice + amortized kernel setup. can also factor in KV cache warmness probability.

rachel: agreed. also add an instrumentation flag to record "kv-cache-warmness" per request in traces so autotuner can learn the real cost.

alex: noted. I'll add the trace field and update the autotuner eval harness. quick wins: A and tiny-fastpath B if needed.

sam: update: first 30m of canary-A looks promising, p95 down ~9% for mixed workloads vs baseline. will post full numbers after 2h. :thumbsup:

alex: great. keep posting. once we have concrete numbers we'll sync on rollout strategy (canary -> staged -> default).

jia: also we should document kernel switch heuristics in eng-runtime/README so on-call knows why we might see transient latency spikes during mixed traffic.

rachel: +1. file an ops note after we finalize thresholds.

alex: thanks team. follow-ups: sam posts canary artifacts, alex posts replay results, jia wires autotuner training metric for kv-warmness.
